title: Tomato leaf spot management
text: Early blight and septoria leaf spot cause dark spots on tomato leaves. Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation before rain, and use copper-based fungicide if disease pressure is high. Treatment cost is typically moderate; delay sprays if heavy rain is forecast within 24 hours.

title: Tomato fertilizer rules
text: Tomato needs balanced NPK. Excess nitrogen increases foliage and disease risk. Prefer split fertilizer doses. With limited budget, prioritize potassium and calcium during fruiting over additional nitrogen.

title: Tomato selling and storage
text: Tomato is perishable with short shelf life. If mandi prices are falling and storage or cold chain is unavailable, consider staged early harvest of ripe fruit rather than holding for a recovery that may not come.

title: Tomato harvest timing
text: Harvest at breaker to pink stage for distant markets; fully ripe for local sale. Morning harvest reduces heat stress. Sort by grade before transport — damaged fruit lowers overall mandi realisation.

title: Potato late blight
text: Late blight thrives in cool wet weather. Scout lower leaves, destroy infected haulms, and apply approved fungicide preventively when rain is expected. Do not spray immediately before heavy rainfall.

title: Potato soil and NPK
text: Potato prefers well-drained loamy soil. Maintain adequate potassium for tuber quality. Avoid waterlogging which raises disease and reduces marketable yield.

title: Potato storage basics
text: Cure tubers in shade for 7–10 days before storage. Store in ventilated structures at 2–4°C if cold storage is available. Sprouting and weight loss increase above 8°C. Check PMFBY coverage before storing large volumes.

title: Onion thrips and bulb quality
text: Thrips cause silvery streaks on leaves and reduce bulb size. Scout weekly during dry spells. Staggered planting reduces peak pest pressure. Harvest when 50–75% tops fall naturally for best storage life.

title: Onion price volatility
text: Onion prices swing sharply with arrival volumes. When prices spike, graded sorting and proper curing improve realisation. During glut, consider value addition (drying) or staggered release if storage is available.

title: Maize nutrient deficiency
text: Yellowing of lower leaves often indicates nitrogen deficiency. Apply urea in splits. Confirm soil moisture before top dressing. Maize responds poorly to drought at tasseling.

title: Maize fall armyworm basics
text: Scout whorls for larvae. Early detection allows mechanical control or targeted insecticide. Avoid blanket sprays when beneficial insects are active.

title: Wheat rust management
text: Yellow and brown rust spread in cool humid conditions. Use resistant varieties where available. Apply fungicide at flag leaf stage if disease exceeds economic threshold. NFSM districts may offer subsidized inputs — check locally.

title: Wheat irrigation critical stages
text: Crown root initiation, tillering, jointing, flowering, and grain filling are sensitive to water stress. One missed irrigation at flowering can cut yield 15–25%. Skip irrigation only when rain exceeds 15 mm.

title: Rice transplanting window
text: Transplant 25–30 day old seedlings at 2–3 seedlings per hill. Maintain 2–5 cm standing water during tillering. Drain briefly before panicle initiation to strengthen roots.

title: Rice stem borer scouting
text: Dead hearts in vegetative stage and white ears at heading indicate stem borer. Monitor weekly. Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids where available before resorting to chemical control.

title: Cotton aphid and whitefly
text: Honeydew from aphids leads to sooty mould. Whitefly transmits leaf curl virus. Avoid repeated broad-spectrum sprays that kill natural enemies. Rotate insecticide modes of action.

title: Irrigation and rain timing
text: Skip irrigation when significant rainfall is forecast. Standing water increases fungal disease risk for tomato and potato. Schedule sprays after rain when leaves dry.

title: Drip irrigation benefits
text: Drip saves 30–50% water versus flood irrigation and reduces weed pressure. PMKSY offers 45–55% subsidy on micro-irrigation. Pair drip with fertigation for better nutrient use efficiency on horticulture crops.

title: Limited budget decision rule
text: Under tight budget, compare treatment cost against expected salvageable yield and current mandi price. If expected post-treatment profit is negative and prices are falling, selling early or reducing input intensity may be safer than full treatment.

title: Soil Health Card usage
text: Test soil every 2 years through the Soil Health Card scheme. Apply nutrients based on recommendations rather than habit. Over-application of nitrogen is a common profit leak on small farms.

title: Crop insurance before risky decisions
text: Enroll in PMFBY before sowing notified crops. Insurance does not replace good agronomy but limits downside when weather or pest causes total loss. Premium is heavily subsidized for most food crops.

title: Sprayer equipment guidance
text: For small farms under 3 acres, knapsack or rental battery sprayers are usually more cost-effective than owning tractor-mounted sprayers. Factor rental into treatment cost.

title: Greenhouse and polyhouse government subsidy (India)
text: Under MIDH/NHM, farmers can get credit-linked back-ended subsidy for polyhouses, greenhouses, and shade-net houses. Baseline central support is often about 50% of admissible project cost for private farmers; many states add top-ups so effective support can be higher for SC/ST, small/marginal, or hilly-area farmers. Application is through the District Horticulture Officer or state horticulture portal. A bank loan is usually required. Subsidy is typically released after construction and inspection, not upfront. Area limits and exact percentages vary by state — confirm on your state horticulture website before applying.

title: Reducing post-harvest losses
text: Sort and grade at harvest. Use clean crates, avoid stacking beyond 4 layers for tomatoes. Cold storage or AIF-backed warehouse loans can improve holding capacity when prices are depressed at peak arrival.
